payload.body: BRIEF, ST0095 (git-style ids), P0. hv's ruling is hv decision 61: threads, work packages and issues go from ordinals to git-style ids based on the creation event's id, everywhere, going forward, with lists ordered by creation time. Existing ids stay as they are. vc writes ST0095's design and work packages NOW for hv's review, and no code lands, and nothing in the tree is written by a seat, until hv has reviewed it. YOUR TASK NOW is read-only: a census in your remit and your positions on the design points below, so the work packages are written from the code and not from memory. RETURN: a file in your own scratchpad, its absolute path sent to vc by SendMessage with a summary of at most 25 lines. Send a partial as soon as you have one if the whole needs more than one pass. Give file:line anchors, a T-shirt size for your part, the risks, and any point you disagree with in your own words: a disagreement goes to hv as you wrote it. ALREADY MEASURED BY vc on brew 3.4.0, so do not repeat it: one person with five merge requests open mints the same number every time (the post-checkout hook takes the other branch's thread out of the store); after the first merge every other branch conflicts in intent/.intentfiles, steel_threads.md and todo.md; `intent sync --apply --yes` refuses while .intentfiles holds conflict markers; the merged result is doctor-clean; the event log keeps one st.new per mint under the old number. vc's DRAFT POSITIONS, yours to correct in your remit: (P1) the id is an abbreviation of a hash of the creation event's id, lowercase hex taken from the front so it lengthens like a git abbreviation, draft 7 characters for a thread and an issue; (P2) a work package gets its own, from its own creation event, unique within its thread and shorter; (P3) existing ordinals stay valid forever, with no alias and no migration; (P4) every list orders by creation time, and an item with no creation event orders by its created date and then its number; (P5) any door takes a unique prefix of an id, case-insensitive, and refuses an ambiguous one with the candidates; (P6) an id already visible in this clone is never issued, and a same-id pair across branches stays git's add/add, repaired by the renumber engine moving one to a fresh id; (P7) id fields that are numbers become strings, the canon schema versions bump, and an older binary refuses the new schema by name. NAMES: nothing Intent keeps names the client, an attendee or the forge's path; write "an attendee's practice repository" and "merge request 8". YOUR CENSUS, ic (shape and transport): every surface that names a thread, work package or issue. At least: the CLI's argument parsers and help; every table and list and what it sorts by; the MCP tools' parameters and descriptions; GraphQL and any REST types (an issue number as an integer); the intent:/// forms; the claim forms ST0000, ST0000/01 and ISSUE:0000; the realised paths under intent/st and intent/issues with .intentfiles' rows; the view templates; errors and remedies that quote an id form; the generated guide; the skills, subagents, rules and templates that teach an id form; docs/ (reference, concepts, the team page's renumber sections) and what hv has asked for by name, a work package that updates the docs for the new ids; surface/ and the Swift app. YOUR POSITIONS: the visible form of each id (prefix, separator, case, length) with how a person says it, types it, and names a branch after it; prefix input and the ambiguity refusal; how ordinals and new ids sit together in one table; what st renumber and issues renumber are called and take once most ids are not numbers; column widths; anything a surface cannot carry.
